chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbat, from his father, that
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked: 'Did the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) used to provide his dependants with a goodly provision?'
He said: 'Yes. The soul, when it recognizes its provision, is content with it and the flesh grows upon it.'

key_terms.اللَّحْم: Flesh, body — here indicating healthy physical growth and well-being
key_terms.عِيَال: Dependants, family members under one's financial responsibility
key_terms.قَنِعَتْ: To be content, to find sufficiency — related to qana'a (contentment) as a virtue
key_terms.قُوت: Provision, sustenance, daily food — the necessary livelihood for dependants
key_terms.مَعْرُوف: That which is recognized as proper and customary; used in fiqh to denote a recognized standard

ai.seo_question: Did the Prophet Muhammad provide adequate provision for his family according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms that the Prophet (SAWW) provided his family with a proper and recognized standard of provision. The Imam then offers a profound insight: the soul, once it has learned and accepted its allotted sustenance, finds contentment and the body flourishes on it. This teaching, rooted in the prophetic model, connects material sufficiency with inner satisfaction — the body thrives not merely from abundance, but from a recognized and accepted provision that the soul is at peace with.
